episodes.title: Dad Mixed Up BOTH Shopping Lists! | Vegetable Market English | Slow Family Story
episodes.story: Maya plans salad and Nina plans soup. Dan combines their color-coded shopping notes, misreads quantities and assigns the right vegetables to the wrong dishes. The children help him ask, check and sort. Everyone cooks together.
episodes.hook: Four versus forty carrots; silent bell pepper; corn with ears; a salad suspiciously resembling soup.
episodes.vocabulary: carrot, tomato, cucumber, zucchini, potato, onion, broccoli, bell pepper, corn, lettuce, cabbage, spinach, basket, list, bag, receipt, change
episodes.grammar: A1: this/these, singular/plural, numbers; A2: some, how many/how much, polite requests, simple past; B1 extension: clarification and because; B2 extension: respectful repair and if + present.
episodes.pronunciation: American tomato, potato, vegetable; first-syllable stress in carrot/cucumber; clear final plural sounds.
episodes.arc: Confidence -> confusion -> admission -> teamwork -> shared meal.
episodes.relative: None; establish all six permanent characters.

episodes.title: Dad Bought the Sourest Fruit! | Fruit Shop English | Funny Slow Story
episodes.story: Dan wants perfect fruit for a family picnic. Max thinks sour means spoiled, and Dan chooses fruit by size alone. A tasting comparison and a budget challenge teach the family to describe what they want.
episodes.hook: A lemon is mistaken for a tiny yellow orange; the biggest fruit will not fit in the picnic basket.
episodes.vocabulary: apple, banana, orange, lemon, lime, grape, strawberry, watermelon, peach, pear, ripe, sour, sweet, peel, slice, pound, bunch
episodes.grammar: A1: colors and likes; A2: comparatives, a bunch of, too/enough; B1: preferences with because; B2: polite alternatives.
episodes.pronunciation: grapes final /s/; ripe versus right; sentence stress in sweeter than.
episodes.arc: Size contest -> sour surprise -> compare carefully -> fruit salad.

episodes.title: Flowers in the Pancakes?! | Kitchen English | Family Comedy
episodes.story: Dan hears flour as flower while helping make breakfast. Maya catches the misunderstanding before anything is added. Nina turns the near-mistake into a kitchen scavenger hunt; the children measure correctly.
episodes.hook: An empty vase waits beside a mixing bowl; Dad asks whether pancakes need a bouquet.
episodes.vocabulary: flour, flower, bowl, whisk, spoon, spatula, measuring cup, batter, pan, stove, plate, egg, milk, butter, pour, stir, flip
episodes.grammar: A1: kitchen nouns and imperatives; A2: count/mass nouns, some/any, first/then; B1: before/after; B2: explaining a misunderstanding.
episodes.pronunciation: flour/flower homophones; whisk initial /w/; pour versus poor varies by accent.
episodes.arc: Misheard word -> check ingredients -> coordinated cooking -> imperfect but tasty breakfast.
episodes.relative: None; adults handle the hot stove.

episodes.title: Dad Tried On the Wrong Shoes! | Shopping Mall English | Slow Story
episodes.story: The family shops for school shoes. Dan confuses his shoe box with Max's, then follows a map upside down. Maya's sister Rose appears briefly to help locate the fitting area, not to solve the whole problem.
episodes.hook: A giant adult foot next to a tiny shoe; Dad calls the escalator a moving staircase and keeps missing the sign.
episodes.vocabulary: mall, entrance, elevator, escalator, store, size, pair, fitting room, shelf, cashier, receipt, refund, tight, loose, comfortable
episodes.grammar: A1: this/that/these/those; A2: sizes, comparative adjectives, can I try; B1: explaining a problem; B2: polite returns.
episodes.pronunciation: shoes /z/ ending; comfortable common American reduction; emphasis in too tight.
episodes.arc: Wrong box -> wrong direction -> ask clearly -> find the right fit.

episodes.title: The Picnic Is on the WRONG Bench! | Park English | Family Adventure
episodes.story: Two similar picnic spots create a harmless mix-up. Dan follows a drawing without checking its orientation. The children use landmarks to find Maya and Nina while keeping together.
episodes.hook: Every bench looks like the bench in Dad's drawing; Max tries to ask a statue for directions.
episodes.vocabulary: park, garden, bench, fountain, path, pond, tree, flowerbed, gate, playground, blanket, picnic basket, shade, left, right, straight
episodes.grammar: A1: where is and place words; A2: prepositions and directions; B1: relative clauses for identifying a bench; B2: checking an interpretation.
episodes.pronunciation: left final cluster; between second-syllable stress; direction phrases with pauses.
episodes.arc: Wrong landmark -> careful observation -> clear directions -> picnic reunion.

episodes.title: Dad Said HOT… But Meant WARM! | Restaurant English | Funny Family Dinner
episodes.story: At a neighborhood restaurant Dan uses hot ambiguously. The server clarifies temperature versus spicy flavor. The family practices ordering, changing an order politely and asking for the check.
episodes.hook: Dan rehearses a grand speech, then only needs: Could I have some water, please?
episodes.vocabulary: menu, server, appetizer, main course, dessert, fork, knife, spoon, napkin, glass, mild, spicy, warm, order, check, takeout box
episodes.grammar: A1: food names; A2: I'd like/could I have; B1: preferences and requests; B2: tactful correction without blame.
episodes.pronunciation: would you connected speech; dessert stress versus desert; clear please.
episodes.arc: Ambiguous order -> clarification -> enjoyable meal -> polite checkout.
episodes.relative: No new relative; server remains a minor supporting role.

episodes.title: Right Bus, Wrong Stop! | Travel English | Slow Family Comedy
episodes.story: The family plans a library trip. Dan reads the departure time correctly but waits at the opposite stop. A quick call with Nina's father Ed helps them describe the direction, then they check the destination sign themselves.
episodes.hook: Dad proudly arrives early at the wrong side of the street; Max wonders whether a bus stop can move.
episodes.vocabulary: bus stop, route, ticket, fare, driver, seat, timetable, destination, arrival, departure, library, block, intersection, umbrella
episodes.grammar: A1: times and numbers; A2: present continuous and going to; B1: future plans and sequencing; B2: confirming travel details.
episodes.pronunciation: thirteen/thirty stress; route accepted American variants; rising checks.
episodes.arc: Good preparation -> wrong assumption -> verify destination -> reach the library.
episodes.relative: Grandpa Ed, Nina's father: 60-second phone cameo.

episodes.title: Grandma's Suitcase Has Everyone's Socks! | Home English | Family Story
episodes.story: Maya's mother Ruth visits. Identical packing cubes mix up the family's laundry. Each person describes ownership and location; Grandma shares a gentle story about Dan's earlier packing mistake.
episodes.hook: Dad claims a tiny sock is a new travel-size fashion; Grandma produces a perfectly labeled checklist.
episodes.vocabulary: suitcase, zipper, drawer, closet, hanger, towel, pillow, blanket, socks, pajamas, laundry, pocket, label, charger, unpack
episodes.grammar: A1: household nouns; A2: possessives and whose; B1: simple past questions; B2: describing evidence and correcting an assumption.
episodes.pronunciation: whose/who's homophones; drawers American rhotic ending; past -ed examples.
episodes.arc: Warm welcome -> mixed belongings -> ownership game -> family memory.
episodes.relative: Grandma Ruth, Maya's mother: 90-120 seconds, then off-screen family visit.

episodes.title: Can Dad Grow Money? | Garden English | Funny Learning Story
episodes.story: The family plants mint, basil and vegetables. Max hears mint and imagines coins; Dan misjudges how much water a pot needs. They read labels, measure water and make a growth journal.
episodes.hook: A pretend paper coin is used as a plant label, not planted; Dad gives a tiny seed a very large name.
episodes.vocabulary: seed, soil, pot, root, stem, leaf, watering can, shovel, sunlight, shade, basil, mint, grow, dry, damp, label
episodes.grammar: A1: plant parts; A2: needs and quantities; B1: if/when and future predictions; B2: explaining a process clearly.
episodes.pronunciation: soil vowel; leaf/leaves consonant change; water common American flap.
episodes.arc: Wordplay -> overconfident gardening -> measured care -> first shared observation.
episodes.relative: Uncle Ben, Dan's brother: a 60-second delivery of empty pots.

episodes.title: The Party Cake Went to the Wrong House! | Everyday English | Family Finale
episodes.story: A smudged house number sends a cake delivery to the neighbor. The family retraces events using descriptions, directions and polite questions. The neighbor returns the cake, and the family celebrates their teamwork.
episodes.hook: Dan has perfect party decorations but no cake; Max volunteers a very small strawberry as the whole dessert.
episodes.vocabulary: invitation, guest, neighbor, address, doorbell, balloons, ribbon, cake, candles, plate, decorations, delivery, mistake, explain, celebrate
episodes.grammar: A1-A2 review; B1: past/present/future contrasts and because; B2: collaborative planning, polite disagreement and repair.
episodes.pronunciation: address noun stress variants; clear house numbers; emphasis on the corrected word.
episodes.arc: Party preparation -> missing cake -> reconstruct and ask -> warm payoff with callbacks.
episodes.relative: Brief returns of Rose and Ed; no large new cast.
